summary.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA reached INR98 crore, but contrast media sales fell on INR30 crore of goods in transit.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR293 crore, up 25% QoQ, led by the PI/API segment as customer destocking eased. Contrast media declined sharply because about INR30 crore of goods in transit at quarter-end will be recognised next quarter, with transit delays from container shortages and geopolitics. Reported gross margin fell about 3 points to 53% on raw material cost increases and mix, while EBITDA margin rose to 33.5% on operating leverage. Management reiterated Vizag Phase 1 (about INR1,000 crore over three years), Mahad Unit 3 commissioning later this calendar year, and the Hyderabad R&D centre becoming operational this month.

segments.name: PI / API (intermediates)
segments.commentary: Main driver of growth; supply of an intermediate restarted after customer destocking in prior quarters. Management says order book is strong and visibility extends for the next 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 40% QoQ, mainly due to goods in transit at quarter-end. Management called the segment stable with long-term arrangements; Q4 FY26 had strong customer off-take.

segments.name: High-intensity sweetener
segments.commentary: Stability and diversification; a new sweetener is in pilot validation at the existing facility, with scale-up planned at Vizag.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the PI/API sales run-rate to be sustainable through FY27, citing the order book and consistent production.
Commercial batches of the iodinated contrast media intermediate expected to start shortly, with positive trend by end-Q2 or start of Q3 FY27.
Mahad Unit 3 (contrast media intermediates) to be commissioned later this calendar year, ahead of earlier H2 FY27 guidance; commercial contribution expected in H2 FY27.
FY27 capex about INR250 crore (company-level FY27 capex guidance of INR400 crore reiterated as similar); about INR1,000 crore over next three years for Vizag Phase 1.
Vizag commercialisation expected from end-FY29 to FY30; ramp-up may take until FY31-FY32.
Management expects to launch 3 contrast media candidates in FY27 and start pilot activity for a new high-intensity sweetener.
Raw material price outlook is uncertain; management will pass cost increases to customers case by case, with a lag of a few quarters.
capex_capacity: Mahad Unit 3 (backward integration for contrast media intermediates): about INR210 crore spent so far, a further INR40 crore committed in the next couple of months; will be capitalised at more than INR200 crore once commercial.

Vizag: about 100 acres secured; consent to establish received; engineering and pre-construction under way. Phase 1 covers contrast media expansion, a multipurpose finishing block, high-intensity sweetener capacity and an intermediate cluster.
Hyderabad R&D centre Phase 1 to be operational in August 2026; talent already onboarded for peptides, GLP-1 intermediates, biocatalysts, flow synthesis and complex pathways.
Plant utilisation about 70% in Q1 FY27 for contrast media; the Mahad line is still in validation.
demand_pricing: PI/API: management cites secular growth in patient prescriptions for the molecule and a strong order book; the call also referenced a recently approved competing oral cholesterol-lowering drug, which management said does not change its order book.

Pricing: no price-increase clause was triggered in Q1. Raw material cost rises (from March 2026) are partly offset by rupee depreciation; price pass-through is being evaluated case by case as the contracts allow.

Pipeline: about 20 high-conviction NCE/RFP opportunities tracked; visibility on 4 chronic-therapy programmes (oncology and CNS among them) in customer development; management expects at least 2 to fructify, with initial volumes small (validation/clinical quantities).
Peptides: strategy focuses on peptide fragments (liquid phase) rather than generic end peptides, to avoid price erosion.
Management declined to name customers or molecules, citing confidentiality agreements, and declined to comment on a competitor's long-term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much contrast media revenue was deferred to Q2, and what is plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Goods in transit at closing were about INR30 crore higher than opening, to be recognised next quarter. Plant utilisation is steady at about 70%, with dispatches at 100% of production.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the jump in other operating income to INR16.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly export incentives linked to export volumes, plus forex gain and higher interest income on mutual fund investments. Management said the ratio to exports should stay in the same range.

qa_highlights.question: Is PI/API volume lumpy or secular?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: end-market demand is growing consistently, and the plant is running steadily with strong order visibility for at least the next 3-4 quarters, though new-molecule trial volumes are small.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase is expected from raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No price-increase clause was triggered in Q1; increases are offset by rupee depreciation and will be passed through case by case with a lag, as the outlook on raw material prices is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset turn outlook as Vizag comes on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag commercialisation starts end-FY29 to FY30 with ramp-up to FY31-32, so no number was given. Current asset turn is high because the asset block is largely depreciated; management expects it to align with industry norms after capitalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mahad facility be used only for captive supply?
qa_highlights.answer: It is for backward integrated intermediates that are currently imported; the line is captive first, with third-party sales possible after stabilisation. It is flexible for contrast media derivatives.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation linked to geopolitics and solvent prices; pass-through timing and extent remain uncertain.
Goods-in-transit and container availability: cut-off timing can swing quarterly contrast media revenue, as seen in Q1.
Concentration in PI/API; management says new molecules will diversify the book but did not quantify the share of new programmes.
Competitive pressure in peptides and from peers' long-term contracts in iodinated contrast media; management declined to comment on specifics.
Mahad commissioning timeline and iodinated contrast media commercial batches (expected by end-Q2 or start of Q3 FY27).
Vizag ramp-up and returns: ramp-up expected only in FY31-FY32; asset turn well below the 3.5-4x historical level in the near term.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order visibility and the long-term platform, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to name customers, molecules, the lateral-entry details or the RFP split, and gave no firm numbers on pricing pass-through or the outlook for the next quarter.

We will not be participating in the front -end generic peptide opportunity where you see cutter and a lot of price erosion.
